title: Storage Account Access Anomalies

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:diagnostics` events with `Category="StorageRead" OR Category="StorageWrite"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.10 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:diagnostics` traffic without `Category="StorageRead" OR Category="StorageWrite"`. Confirm UC-4.2.10 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="StorageRead" OR Category="StorageWrite"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.10_storage_account_access_a_10"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.10 — Storage Account Access Anomalies: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:diagnostics` for search criteria `Category="StorageRead" OR Category="StorageWrite"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Storage Account Access Anomalies' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.10 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable storage diagnostic logging. Baseline normal access patterns. Alert on volumetric anomalies (unusual number of reads/writes) or new source IPs.
visualization: Table (IP, account, operations), Line chart (access over time), Map.
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable storage diagnostic logging. Baseline normal access patterns. Alert on volumetric anomalies (unusual number of reads/writes) or new source IPs.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="StorageRead" OR Category="StorageWrite"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.10_storage_account_access_a_10"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:diagnostics` in `index=azure` to detect storage account access anomalies. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_10_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (IP, account, operations), Line chart (access over time), Map..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of storage account access anomalies so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
